Exploratory transformation-based PCA of vegetation communities

Source: R/tb_pca_plot.R
tb_pca_plot.Rd

Performs an unconstrained principal component analysis (PCA) on a Hellinger- or chord-transformed vegetation matrix. Produces coordinated ordination plots of sites and selected species, coloured according to previously defined vegetation groups.

Usage

tb_pca_plot(
  veg,
  groups,
  transformation = c("hellinger", "chord"),
  axes = c(1, 2),
  area = c("hull", "ellipse", "none"),
  species = c("ordiselect", "indval", "phi"),
  indval = NULL,
  phi = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  ablim = 0.4,
  fitlim = 0.5,
  freq = FALSE,
  label_groups = FALSE,
  segment.alpha_labelSpe = 0.3,
  segment.size_labelSpe = 0.3
)

Arguments

veg

Numeric matrix or data frame with sites in rows and species in columns. Must have site row names, non-negative values, and no NA.

groups

Data frame containing stand (site identifier) and group (group membership). Every site in veg must appear exactly once in groups.

transformation

Character string; "hellinger" (default) or "chord".

axes

Integer vector of length two specifying distinct PCA axes to plot; defaults to c(1, 2).

area

Character string indicating group envelopes for the site plot: "hull" (default), "ellipse", or "none".

species

Character string specifying species selection: "ordiselect" (default), "indval", or "phi".

indval

Complete indicspecies::multipatt() result for IndVal selection; required when species = "indval".

phi

Complete indicspecies::multipatt() result for Phi-type selection (typically func = "r.g"); required when species = "phi".

alpha

Numeric significance threshold for selecting species from indval or phi; default 0.05.

ablim

Proportion of most abundant species considered by goeveg::ordiselect(); default 0.4.

fitlim

Proportion of species retained based on their ordination scores by goeveg::ordiselect(); default 0.5.

freq

Logical; if TRUE, ordiselect uses species frequencies rather than abundances; default FALSE.

label_groups

Logical; if TRUE, displays group-centroid labels on the site plot and adds group IDs to species labels; default FALSE.

segment.alpha_labelSpe

Numeric transparency of the label connector segments in the species plot; default 0.3.

segment.size_labelSpe

Numeric line width of the label connector segments in the species plot; default 0.3.

Value

A list with the following elements:

pca

PCA object returned by vegan::rda().

plot_sites

ggplot2 plot of the site ordination.

plot_species

ggplot2 plot of selected species scores.

sites

Data frame with site IDs, plot coordinates, and groups.

species

Data frame with selected species, plot coordinates, and assigned groups.

selected_species

Character vector of selected species names.

variance

Numeric vector of variance explained by each PCA axis, expressed as a percentage.

Details

The vegetation matrix must contain sites (releves) in rows and species in columns, with non-negative numeric values and unique site row names. The groups data frame must have columns stand and group, and its site identifiers must match those in veg. Group order is matched to the vegetation matrix automatically. At least two groups and no empty sites are required; species absent from every site are removed.

For transformation = "hellinger", the data are transformed using vegan::decostand(method = "hellinger"). With "chord", the function uses vegan::decostand(method = "normalize", MARGIN = 1). Unconstrained PCA is then performed using vegan::rda(); site and species scores are extracted with scaling = 2.

Site groups can be displayed as convex hulls (area = "hull"), 95-percent normal-data ellipses ("ellipse"), or points alone ("none"). Hulls require at least three non-collinear observations per group, whereas ellipses require at least four non-collinear observations. Ellipses describe the spread of sites and are not confidence intervals for group centroids.

Three species-selection methods are available:

  • "ordiselect": selects species using goeveg::ordiselect() with ablim, fitlim, and freq. Species are coloured by the group with the highest mean cover, a descriptive criterion.

  • "indval": uses significant single-group associations from a previously computed indicspecies::multipatt() result.

  • "phi": uses significant single-group associations from a previously computed multipatt() result (typically with func = "r.g").

For "indval" and "phi", the supplied multipatt object must contain the same ordered site-group assignments as the PCA input. Species are selected by p.value <= alpha and membership of exactly one group; the function does not apply a separate minimum Phi cutoff or adjust p-values for multiple testing.

When label_groups = TRUE, group labels are added at site centroids and appended to species labels. Species are displayed as text labels with optional label connector segments; the species-arrow drawing code is commented out in this implementation.

References

Legendre, P. & Gallagher, E. D. (2001). Ecologically meaningful transformations for ordination of species data. Oecologia, 129, 271-280. https://doi.org/10.1007/s004420100716

See also

vegan::decostand(), vegan::rda(), vegan::scores(), goeveg::ordiselect(), indicspecies::multipatt()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("dune", package = "vegan")
data("dune.env", package = "vegan")

# Create a group-membership table, matching the vegetation matrix
site_groups <- data.frame(
  stand = rownames(dune),
  group = as.character(dune.env$Management)
)

# Hellinger PCA with convex hulls and ordiselect
res <- tb_pca_plot(
  veg = dune,
  groups = site_groups,
  transformation = "hellinger",
  area = "hull",
  species = "ordiselect"
)
print(res$plot_sites)
print(res$plot_species)
res$selected_species

# Alternative chord transformation with group labels
res_chord <- tb_pca_plot(
  veg = dune,
  groups = site_groups,
  transformation = "chord",
  area = "none",
  label_groups = TRUE
)

# Previously computed IndVal indicators
set.seed(123)
mp_indval <- indicspecies::multipatt(
  (dune > 0) * 1,
  site_groups$group,
  duleg = TRUE,
  control = permute::how(nperm = 999)
)
res_indval <- tb_pca_plot(
  veg = dune,
  groups = site_groups,
  species = "indval",
  indval = mp_indval
)
} # }
